text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Clinton Wins.
- Suspicion in Foreign Ministry ministers will cancel participation in Cairo economic conference.
MAARIV
- Clinton leads.
- Netanyahu's secret plan: negotiations will stop in case of suicide attack.
- US envoy Dennis Ross cancelled Israel trip at last minute due to difficulties in Hebron talks.
- Estimate: population to reach 6.2 million in 2000.
JERUSALEM POST
- Clinton confident as America votes.
- US to confer major non-NATO status on Jordan.
- Israeli businessmen dropping out of Cairo conference.
- Africa-Israel bidders include US tycoon Ronald Lauder, diamond businessman Laviev.
- Foreign investment rose 7.3 percent in first eight months.
- Knesset committee supports boost to minimum wage.
HAARETZ
- Projections at close of US polling: Clinton victory.
- Security source: No escape from investigation of Panther helicopter sales in New York.
- Treasury: Cancel advantages of Israeli companies in public tenders.
- Treasury proposal: Start-up technology companies to continue to receive state guarantees.
GLOBES
- Only 3 groups in Africa-Israel tender. Estimate: Laviev proposal highest.
- Results of tender on international calls today. Estimate: Gold Line group among one of two winners.
- Estimates of Pelephone value: 1.8 to 2.25 billion dollars.
- Savings in economy dropped by 65 percent in five years.
